authors: Andraž De Luisa; Jan Hartman; David Nabergoj; Samo Pahor; Marko Rus; Bozhidar Stevanoski; Jure Demšar; Erik Štrumbelj
title: Predicting the Popularity of Games on Steam
read_scope: Sections 2, 3.1, 4.2 and conclusion; targeted full-text reading
data_and_sample: 8,000 games released after 2015; Steam, SteamSpy and SteamDB; collected December 2020.
target_and_timing: Second-month median player count, using first-month player count; explicitly post-release.
features: Past players, price, language count, storage, release-time features and genre structure.
split_and_baselines: PSIS approximation to leave-one-game-out; normal, folded-normal and hierarchical Bayesian variants.
metrics: LOO information criterion and posterior predictive checks; not comparable to our tier macro-F1.
limitations: Does not establish pre-release prediction or unseen-developer performance.
our_decision: Keep observation timing explicit; exclude player-count signals from planning feature set. Our owners classification answers a different question.

title: Mobile games success and failure: mining the hidden factors
read_scope: Sections 3.1-3.3, 4.2 and limitations; targeted full-text reading
data_and_sample: Over 17,000 Apple App Store games, August 2019; originally 18 attributes.
target_and_timing: Constructed success score plus rating-average/count classifications; existing-store metadata, proposed use before release.
features: Genre, languages, IAPs, developer maturity and release attributes among considered metadata.
split_and_baselines: 80/10/10 train/validation/test; compares SVM, random forest and ANN. Developer-disjoint split not established in inspected description.
metrics: Classification accuracy around 70% reported; confusion matrices.
limitations: Apple-only scope; composite-score parameters include judgment. Exact score is not adopted here.
our_decision: Supports studying metadata but not calling Android installs revenue or importing the composite score. Use independent Android labels and developer groups.

title: Data Analysis and Success Prediction of Mobile Games before Publishing on Google Play Store
venue: International Journal of Education and Management Engineering 14(3), 13-21
read_scope: Abstract, sections 3 and 5, tables 3-7; full PDF text inspected
data_and_sample: Abstract discusses Google Play and >17,000 games; section 3 instead describes >20,000 Apple App Store games with 21 attributes and January 2023 collection.
target_and_timing: Predicted downloads/ratings compared with developer targets; pre-publication claim.
features: Section 5 lists category, publisher and price/free state; section 3.3 includes outcome fields in a broader feature description.
split_and_baselines: RF, Naive Bayes, KNN and SVM; reproducible split and feature/target separation not established in inspected sections.
metrics: Claims RF accuracy 98.82%; evaluation description does not provide a sufficiently clear comparable protocol.
limitations: Internal platform/sample and feature-description inconsistencies; cannot diagnose actual training leakage without code.
our_decision: Contextual related work with unresolved evidence quality; do not adopt its accuracy as a benchmark or pre-release guarantee.

title: Leakage and the reproducibility crisis in machine-learning-based science
read_scope: Publisher indexed abstract, bibliographic metadata and arXiv abstract; PMC full-text access blocked
data_and_sample: Methodological review and reproducibility investigation, not a game cohort.
target_and_timing: Data-leakage-related validity of ML research claims.
features: Not applicable as a game feature specification.
split_and_baselines: Detailed case-study implementation not assessed in this reading; no game baseline inferred.
limitations: This reading supports the general concern, not a claim that every compared paper leaks.
our_decision: Track cohort, predictor timing and split provenance. Operational implementation additionally follows official scikit-learn guidance.

title: Evaluating the effectiveness of explanations for recommender systems: Methodological issues and empirical studies on the impact of personalization
read_scope: Publisher abstract and metadata only; full empirical methods not inspected
data_and_sample: Explanation evaluation; participant counts not established in this reading.
target_and_timing: Decision effectiveness and its relationship with satisfaction, among explanation goals.
features: Explanation design, not game popularity predictors.
split_and_baselines: No experimental details inferred from abstract.
metrics: Abstract distinguishes explanation goals; exact task metrics need full-method review before replication.
limitations: Does not validate our interface or justify equating user satisfaction with decision quality.
our_decision: Separate task correctness/completion from satisfaction in planned FYP user evaluation.

authors: Kathrin Wardatzky; Oana Inel; Luca Rossetto; Abraham Bernstein
title: Whom do Explanations Serve? A Systematic Literature Survey of User Characteristics in Explainable Recommender Systems Evaluation
venue: arXiv preprint; this record uses v1, not an assumed later publication
read_scope: Abstract, section 3 selection/annotation, section 4 results and section 5 recommendations; targeted reading
target_and_timing: Whose experience is represented in explanation evaluations.
features: Participant demographics, experience and other user characteristics.
split_and_baselines: Literature survey, not a train/test game experiment.
metrics: Patterns of participant reporting and explanation effects; no game accuracy benchmark.
limitations: Does not establish that a particular explanation will improve our users' decisions.
our_decision: Record recruitment, gaming/development and data-literacy experience; limit generalization if participants are convenience-sampled students.
